row_statement: Conjecture 2 of Horsch (every graph has an orientation that maximizes total arc-connectivity and is well-balanced in the sense of Nash-Williams) is false: for an explicit simple graph on 8 vertices with 14 edges, one orientation has total arc-connectivity at least 75, while every well-balanced orientation has at most 74, so no maximizing orientation is well-balanced. Lean also proves that well-balanced orientations of the witness exist.

round2-final-check-358412-sol61-20261120-r1/FINAL-REVIEW-358412.md (GPT-6.1 Sol: PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; no definition issue; independent max-flow confirms 75 versus 74; eligibility doubt on the unread journal text only)

round2-confirm-G13-opus-20261120-r1/CONFIRM.md (Claude Opus 5.5: CONFIRMED_TIER2, confidence 0.88; max-flow over all 2^14 orientations: 44 maximizers at 75, none well-balanced; 432 well-balanced orientations with maximum 74; Lean definitions match the source one for one)
caveats: The journal text (Theoretical Computer Science 978 (2023) 114176) is unread. Open record: arXiv v2 of 2023-08-30 is the latest version, the journal DOI was created ten days later, and the journal's 17 references match v2's in order; so v2 is almost certainly the accepted text.

The witness is a smallest simple counterexample (Opus: none on 7 or fewer vertices; none on 8 vertices with 13 or fewer edges; exactly 7 of the 1,579 connected graphs with 8 vertices and 14 edges fail). A computer search finds one in minutes; the source states no tested range.
The source's own tripled-path example does not contradict the conjecture (checked).
sweep_verdict: NO_PRIOR_FOUND (arXiv v2; one citing paper in OpenAlex, on a different objective; none of Horsch's 26 later works touches the question; Principia; six omega issue searches with a working control query; web searches)
